 KRA Sets November 30 Deadline for Multinationals to Declare 15% Tax Status 
 -->
 --> 
 by Timothy Cerullo on Monday, 9 November 2026 - 11:43 am 
 Times Tower 
 Kenyans.co.ke 
 -->
 The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has given multinational companies operating in Kenya 21 days to declare whether they are covered by a new tax that requires large companies to pay at least 15 per cent tax on their profits. 
 In a notice dated Monday, November 9, KRA directed companies covered by the Minimum Top-Up Tax (MTT) to notify the Commissioner of their status by November 30, 2026. 
 KRA directed the affected companies to provide the name of their multinational group, the country where its main company is based, and details of all related companies operating in Kenya, including their KRA PINs. 
 "Notify the Commissioner of being in scope, including the group name, Country of the Ultimate Parent Entity, and a listing of Constituent entities in Kenya with their PINs," KRA directed. 
 An undated image of customers lining up for services at KRA's offices. 
 Photo 
 Sacco Review 
 The tax applies to multinational companies whose combined annual revenue is at least Ksh110 billion in at least two of the previous four financial years. 
 This means that a Kenyan subsidiary of an international company could be affected even if its own annual revenue is below Ksh110 billion, provided the entire multinational group meets the required revenue threshold. 
 Besides declaring their tax status, the affected companies must also file Minimum Top-Up Tax returns and pay any additional tax due under the new regime. 
 “We therefore wish to inform all taxpayers covered in the scope of the MTT to file a return for declaration of MTT and pay any minimum top-up tax due,” the Authority added. 
 KRA further directed the companies to comply with the Multilateral Competent Authority Agreement on the Exchange of GloBE Information, which allows tax authorities in different countries to share information about multinational businesses. 
 The Minimum Top-Up Tax is designed to ensure that large multinational companies pay a tax rate of at least 15 per cent on their profits in countries where they operate. 
 Under the arrangement, companies whose effective tax rate falls below 15 per cent may be required to pay additional tax to cover the difference, subject to adjustments provided under the regulations. 
 Th e tax was introduced through the Tax Laws (Amendment) Act, 2024 , which added Section 12G to the Income Tax Act, before KRA issued regulations in 2026 to guide its implementation. 
 The regulations were published through Legal Notice Number 189 on September 18, 2026, outlining how the tax would be implemented and the obligations of companies covered by the law.
